title: Your first compose.yaml
summary: Write the docker run commands for greet into a compose.yaml, and start the web page and the say program with one command.

tasks.title: `compose.yaml` exists and Compose can read it
tasks.hint: Make a file called `compose.yaml`. Indentation matters: two spaces per level, never tabs. `docker compose config` shows what Compose understood, or the line it can't read.

tasks.title: Service `web` is built from this folder and running
tasks.hint: Under `services:`, a `web:` with `build: .`. Then `docker compose up -d`.

tasks.title: `http://localhost:3500` greets you (not "friend") on a pink page
tasks.hint: Give `web` `ports:` `- "3500:3000"` and `environment:` with `NAME: <your name>` and `COLOR: pink`. After changing the file, `docker compose up -d` again.

tasks.title: Service `say` ran `say.js` and printed hello
tasks.hint: A second service from the same folder: `say:` with `build: .` and `command: ["node", "say.js"]`. `docker compose logs say` shows what it printed.
